6000000006.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) are valid for sound batts. The GWP may vary between 0.7-1.6 kg CO₂e/kg based on the manufacturer. The average data values are based on EPDs from the following countries (in order of assumed market share): Sweden, Germany and Poland.
6000000006.Name: Glasswool, sound batts
6000000006.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal to the construction it is part of.
6000000006.Synonyms: Glass wool, mineral glass wool, mineral wool, batts, boards, panels, acoustic, sound, noice reduction
6000000006.TechnologicalApplicability: Glass wool is normally used as thermal insulation, but this product type is primarily used for sound insulation. Glass wool is intended for use in a protected environment.
6000000006.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Glass wool is produced in an electric furnace. The process involves primary raw materials and energy sources, both of which contribute to the GWP. The proportion of recycled glass used as raw material varies between 40 and 80%. The amount of binder is approximately 5 to 10%. There is a minor variation in density for the same lambda value between different manufacturers, but the density values given here, as well as the lambda value, are representative of the products used on the Swedish market.
6000000006.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that are currently consumed on the Swedish market.
6000000006.UseAdviceForDataSet: The product type glasswool, sound batts, includes all types of sound insulation with a density for use sound insulation and do not include any surfacing. In the case that surfacing is included, a more precise and exact choice should be made; such products typically have higher climate impact per kg.

6000000007.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producers, which is why the background data used from Swedish sawmills can be considered representative of this consumption.
6000000007.ComparativeProperty: When the products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective.
6000000007.GeneralComment: Input are collected from 44 sawmills and cover the production of 10 190 000 m³ sawn dried timber. Data to produce sawn wood is collected from a representative selection of sawmills in Sweden and weighted to an average. Sawn dried timber that is produced in Sweden is mainly based on domestic logs. The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for sawn timbers varies between 21-37 kg CO₂e/m³ for the companies that are involved (and based on the methodology and inventory data used).
6000000007.Name: Sawn timber, u 16 %, coniferous
6000000007.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of wood indoors is normally equal to the construction of which it is part of. Wood exposed to outdoors normally needs maintenance during these 50 years lifespan.
6000000007.TechnologicalApplicability: Sawn timber can be used directly as it is and serves as a raw material for impregnated wood. When it is planed, it is used for other wood-based products. Sawn timber is used in construction for formwork and structural timber, for so-called cladding timber for panels, as well as planed for flooring or joinery timber for windows, doors, and interior fittings, etc. The wood is usually refined by planing, profiling, gluing, finger-jointing, or impregnation depending on the area of use.
6000000007.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The climate impact is based on a sector EPD that cover 58 % of the total sawn softwood timber in Sweden. Dried sawn timber has an average density of 455 kg/m³ and moisture content of 16 %. Sawn dried timber of spruce has an average density of 470 kg/m³ and 440 kg/m³ for pine. The moisture content for the dried wood is about 12-18 %. Biogenic carbon storage is 715kg CO₂/m³.
6000000007.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the major producers and thereby the major consumption of sawn timber used in Sweden. These data represent the year 2020, i.e. after reduction diesel was implemented why the GWP reported is lower than before.
6000000007.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative of sawn dried timber and can be used as it is, but is mainly used as a raw material in planed wood production.

6000000023.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is partly covered by national production, but significant imports come mainly from Finland and other nearby countries.
6000000023.ComparativeProperty: The specific board is designed to be used indoors and has a common thickness of 12 mm.
6000000023.GeneralComment: GWP (A1-A3) for wood-based panels can vary greatly between different manufacturers. To achieve a comment result, the biogenic carbon stored in products is subtracted, so that the climate impact is reported as GWP-GHG. Even after this, there can be significant differences between manufacturers which, without access to the underlying LCA report, are difficult to explain. One difference may be the environmental impact allocated to the wood raw material. For plywood, climate impact has thus been corrected for a producer (i.e. reduced). The difference after correction is less than 10 % between producers.
6000000023.Name: Plywood (spruce or pine)
6000000023.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of the product is normally equal to the service life of the construction of which it is a part of.
6000000023.TechnologicalApplicability: Plywood is commonly used as a surface material in a protected environment from weather exposure or indoors. Plywood is available as unclassified building plywood and as classified structural plywood. Structural plywood is used, for example, behind plasterboards in standard stud walls to allow heavier items to be screwed onto the finished wall. Structural plywood is manufactured in two different classes: 15/50 and 20/70 (bending strength in MPa/modulus of elasticity in MPa).
6000000023.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Data is valid for plywood made of spruce or pine and about 10 % resin . Densities between different producers varies +/-5 %.
6000000023.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing processes and products that are currently consumed on the market. Data are valid until new ones are published.
6000000023.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data are representative of a plywood consisting of thin wood veneers that are cross-laminated, glued, heat-treated, and pressed under high pressure. This results in a dimensionally stable and strong board.

6000000029.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Concrete manufacturers are spread across the entire country, and the environmental data can be considered representative since the concrete recipes used, as well as the binder mix, reflect the production of all these manufacturers and are also based on several EPDs.
6000000029.ComparativeProperty: When concrete products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, i.e. the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
6000000029.GeneralComment: Concrete is made from rock, gravel and cement where the main raw material is limestone. In climate-improved concrete is part of the cement replaced with alternative binders. The data given, based on compressive strength class, represent commonly used concrete recipes on the market. Factory data for module A3 is based on data from a large number of EPDs. Of the reported value for climate impact, the contribution from the manufacturing process (A3) is relatively small in relation to the contribution from the cement, which normally accounts for more than 90 % of the concrete's climate impact in module A1-A3. Environmental data for the cement binders used are based on EPDs for commonly used cement grades on the Swedish market.
6000000029.Name: Ready-mix made concrete, buildings C25/30
6000000029.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: Concrete exposed to outdoors or other wet environment is designed in respect to durability according to Eurocodes. The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of. Concrete for buildings usually does not need any maintenance during its dimensioned service life.
6000000029.TechnologicalApplicability: Concrete for houses is used especially for load-bearing parts of the structure. The concrete composition is controlled, in addition to compressive strength of exposure class, but also of other properties e.g. consistence, time for curing and drying.
6000000029.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The compressive strength class of the concrete follows the standard EN 206:2013+A1:2016 and SS 137003:2015.
6000000029.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The provided data are representative of the Swedish producers of ready-mixed concrete and the concrete recipes they use. This information was collected in 2020. The environmental impact data are based on current EPDs for binders as well as factory data.
6000000029.UseAdviceForDataSet:
The compressive strength classes refer to concrete used for buildings with a concrete composition and binder mix representative of the Swedish market. If more properties are required for a concrete, information from a supplier must be used. Normally, concrete is reinforced. Reinforcement is handled as a separate resource in this database.
For testing compressive strength, EN 206 refers to the following standard: EN 12390-3, Testing hardened concrete — Part 3: Compressive strength of test specimens. In Table 12 of EN 206 specifies "Compressive strength classes for normal concrete and heavy concrete". This is supplemented in SS 137003 with "Table 1 — Intermediate classes for compressive strength".

6000000082.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: All bricks used in Sweden are imported (the last brickyard was located at Haga, Enköping and was closed in 2020. A very small production based on old technology is nowadays left at Horns Tegelbruk). The largest imports come from Denmark and then from Finland, the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany.
6000000082.ComparativeProperty: When bricks are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
6000000082.GeneralComment: Bricks are manufactured of clay, sand, lime and sawdust. The bricks are burned in a tunnel furnace at a high temperature, roughly 1050 degrees. The primary energy use varies between 2.0 – 4 MJ/kg of nonrenewable energy and 0.5 MJ/kg of electricity. The use of combustion of fossil fuels is the dominant contribution to the products GHG emissions. Environmental data are based EPD for suppliers to the domestic Swedish market.
6000000082.Name: Bricks
6000000082.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of. Bricks in buildings usually does not need any maintenance during its dimensioned service life. Bricks are suitable for reuse.
6000000082.TechnologicalApplicability: Bricks are normally used in Sweden without glaze and different size occurs from different producers and common standard formats is produced as well (228x108x54 mm). Brick can be used for load bearing structures or for decorative and functional purpose when used exterior or interior. Brick is used indoor in interior walls, but is not so common in Sweden. Facing bricks is a modern alternative as facade cladding.
6000000082.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The technology used by the manufacturers is similar, but the fuel varies, with natural gas and oil being predominant. An addition of limestone powder to the clay produces yellow bricks. For brown or brown-black bricks, manganese is used. Roof tiles are fired in cassettes at 1050°C. The firing process itself takes two days in a modern tunnel kiln. The entire process is monitored to ensure that all roof tiles achieve uniform hardness and are frost-resistant.
6000000082.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data given are representative of the bricks that are consumed on the Swedish market. Environmental data is based on the producers EPD collected during 2020.
6000000082.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data are representative for bricks used on the Swedish market.

6000000140.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The manufacturing is done by heating the raw materials (bitumen and copolymers) to a specific temperature and mixing them. After this the mix is applied to the reinforcing structure (polyester or glass fibre). The resulting sheet is cooled and then faced with mineral granules. The bitumen is generally delivered as hot from the petroleum refinery to the manufacturing site, where it’s heated further. Significant differences arise mainly from the amounts of bitumen and the SBS used in the products. As SBS has a large share of emission, using alternative copolymers to modify the bitumen would also change the GWP-GHG A1-A3 value.
6000000140.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The information is representative of the manufacturers of bitumen waterproofing layers and the products consumed on the Swedish market. Data are representative for a PYE top layer bitumen waterproofing membrane used on the Swedish market. In the Nordic countries is bitumen waterproofing almost exclusively uses bitumen modified with SBS (styrene-butadiene-styrene).
